clue.text: German brought in to give tour of fair venue

indicators.note: the German letter is brought in between the other two pieces, set inside them

parts.note: to show something can mean to give or present it
a round is a tour of calls or visits

explanation.surface: A German is brought along to be shown round a fair's site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in' puts G between the two synonyms, not inside a single word.
explanation.definitionFit: A showground is the open site where agricultural shows and fairs are held.

clue.text: Poor sci-fi turned out to be dull

indicators.note: something turned out is overturned and rearranged, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A poor science-fiction story proved boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' rearranges the letters of POOR SCIFI.
explanation.definitionFit: Something soporific sends you to sleep, so it is tedious and boring.

clue.text: Chap in boat, a second seen round river in Arab state

indicators.note: the inner letters sit in the middle of the Gulf country's name

parts.note: Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula

indicators.note: the first pair is seen wrapped round the river letter

explanation.surface: A man in a boat is spotted circling a river in the Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen round' puts R inside AS to give ARS, which goes in OMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A rower is a man who pulls an oar in a boat.

clue.text: Song identifying salad items one's merely heard

indicators.note: the clue says the phrase is only spoken, so it is a sound-alike and not a spelling

parts.note: greens and leaves are both salad ingredients

explanation.surface: Someone names a tune from a list of salad ingredients overheard.
explanation.walkthrough: GREENS LEAVES spoken aloud matches the title; the second word is spelt SLEEVES.
explanation.definitionFit: Greensleeves is a famous traditional English folk tune.

clue.text: Work beginning to thrill? The writer's repeatedly nursing source of some hope

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word thrill is taken

parts.note: the writer's means the writer is, I'M

indicators.note: the doubled contraction holds the extra letter inside it, as if nursing it

parts.note: repeatedly asks for the writer's contraction a second time, I'M again

indicators.note: the first letter of the word some is its source

explanation.surface: A work starting with a thrill; the author repeatedly cherishes the root of some hope.
explanation.walkthrough: I'M twice gives IMIM; 'nursing' puts S inside the second I'M, making IMISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimism is a hopeful outlook, so hope is a near synonym.

clue.text: Stupid new hanger-on missing opening

definitions.note: used as a noun, as in calling someone 'stupid', a fool

indicators.note: the hanger-on word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a poodle is a servile follower or lackey

explanation.surface: A dim new follower lacking a way in.
explanation.walkthrough: POODLE loses its P to give OODLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodle is informal for a silly person, a fool.

clue.text: Recalled expression of surprise with church having acoustic feature

indicators.note: called back, so the joined pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: oh is an exclamation of surprise
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A cry of surprise remembered in a church with notable acoustics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' turns OHCE round to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a reflected sound, a feature of a building's acoustics.

clue.text: Advice to have effect mostly on individual? Mostly

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: to count is to matter or have effect

indicators.note: again the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: self means an individual person

explanation.surface: Guidance that mostly works on a single person, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: COUNT and SELF each lose a last letter: COUN + SEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel is guidance or recommendation given to someone.

clue.text: Picked up some rare Poulenc stage work

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted, read upward from bottom
only some of the letters of the phrase are used, sitting inside it

explanation.surface: Someone gets hold of a rare stage piece by the composer Poulenc.
explanation.walkthrough: AREPO sits in 'rARE POulenc'; 'Picked up' reads it upward. 'Picked up' could suggest a sound-alike; here it is a lift.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a dramatic work set to music and staged.

clue.text: Positive force in building? That's the ideal state

indicators.note: the force letter goes inside the building word

parts.note: an erection is a building or structure
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: A query about a beneficial influence in construction, called the ideal.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfection is the condition of being flawless, the ideal.

clue.text: Pipe came up with lumps or swellings

definitions.note: an adjective here; tuberose also means tuberous

parts.note: a tube is a pipe
rose means came up

explanation.surface: A pipe surfaced covered in lumps.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is usually a flowering plant; here it is the rarer adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuberose as an adjective means bearing tubers, knobbly with swellings.

clue.text: Working in that place leads to restriction that's reactive

parts.note: on means working, as in a machine switched on
there means in that place
a bound is a limit or restriction

explanation.surface: Operating somewhere leads to a limit that responds.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting on the rebound is reacting to a recent setback, especially a broken romance.

clue.text: Japanese broth recipe's the last word

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin
amen is the last word of a prayer

explanation.surface: A Japanese broth recipe is the definitive version.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramen is a Japanese noodle soup in a rich stock.

clue.text: Rejected intent to import English ways in Pacific region

indicators.note: the turned word takes the other pieces inside it, importing them
rejected means sent back, so the word reads in reverse

parts.note: aim means intent
lanes are ways or roads

explanation.surface: Turned-down plans to bring English roads to a Pacific area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' turns AIM to MIA; ELANES goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Melanesia is the group of islands in the south-west Pacific including Fiji.

clue.text: Fellow among celebrities is a top performer

parts.note: in means among
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: A man surrounded by famous people is a star turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A finalist has reached the last round, one of the best competitors.

clue.text: Villa well placed in court

indicators.note: the well word is placed inside the court abbreviation

parts.note: hale means well, healthy

explanation.surface: A villa well located in a courtyard.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalet is a holiday house, like a villa.

clue.text: Property document: hint of trouble it conveyed about river

indicators.note: only a hint, the first letter, of the word trouble is used
the conveyed word wraps about the river

parts.note: led means conveyed, guided
the Dee is a river in Wales and England, and in Scotland

explanation.surface: A deed with a hint of trouble, passed on around a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a river on the England-Wales border; 'about' wraps the conveyed word round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A title deed is the legal record proving ownership of land or a house.

clue.text: Endless worry? Lifted it with classical pieces

indicators.note: the worry word loses its end letter

parts.note: concern means worry

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means read upward

explanation.surface: An unending worry lifted with classical music.
explanation.definitionFit: Concerti are classical compositions for a soloist with orchestra.

clue.text: Scoundrel receiving award from Queen leads to trouble

definitions.note: a verb here, to trouble or hamper

indicators.note: the scoundrel word receives the award inside it

parts.note: a cur is a scoundrel
the MBE is a British honour granted by the monarch

explanation.surface: A rogue's royal honour causes problems.
explanation.definitionFit: To cumber is to hinder or burden, an old word for encumber.

clue.text: Welsh location is unclear

definitions.meaning: a headland and district near Swansea in South Wales
speaks indistinctly, is unclear in speech

explanation.surface: A Welsh place is hard to make out.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech said quietly and indistinctly is unclear; the Mumbles is a resort area in Wales.

clue.text: Meal parts too well cooked?

indicators.note: well cooked suggests the letters are thoroughly mixed and reworked

explanation.surface: A query whether pieces of the dinner are overdone.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot roast is a dish of braised meat, a meal.

clue.text: A conclusion to fighting securing one success for former Emperor

indicators.note: the knockout letters secure the other pieces inside them

parts.note: KO, a knockout, ends a boxing fight
I is the Roman numeral one
a hit is a success

explanation.surface: A victory that ends the fighting brings success for an ex-ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conclusion to fighting' looks like G, the last letter; it is KO.
explanation.definitionFit: Akihito was Emperor of Japan until he abdicated in 2019.

clue.text: Regretted involving Government after American put the case

indicators.note: the regret piece is written after the American letter
the regret word wraps round the government letter

parts.note: rued means regretted

explanation.surface: An American who regretted a government role then made an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: To have argued is to have presented reasons, putting the case.

clue.text: My son returned in a measured way, completing a sort of pattern?

definitions.note: the answer completes the phrase 'a ___ pattern'

indicators.note: returned means sent back, read in reverse

parts.note: metric relates to measuring, in measure

explanation.surface: A parent says the son came back in an orderly way, finishing a design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' makes SYM; the question mark flags the fill-in-the-blank definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A symmetric pattern is balanced, its halves mirroring each other.

clue.text: Pipe we included in series

indicators.note: the word we is included inside the series abbreviation

explanation.surface: A pipe we fitted into a sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: A sewer is a drain or pipe carrying waste.

clue.text: Happen to catch free union member

indicators.note: the happen word catches the other inside it

parts.note: to be means to happen, take place
rid means free, as in rid of

explanation.surface: Chance to grab a free member of a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union member' looks like trade unions; it is marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride is one of the two partners in a marriage, a union.

clue.text: Healthy expression of group intent

definitions.meaning: ..., short for we will, states what a group plans

explanation.surface: A healthy statement of a team's plans.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well is being in good health; we'll declares a collective intention.

clue.text: Component of program revised by best in our university

indicators.note: revised means reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Part of a computer program rewritten by the brightest at our university.
explanation.definitionFit: A subroutine is a self-contained section of code within a larger program.

clue.text: See 10
Hero of novel: edition, with twist, reversed opening

parts.note: to wind is to twist

indicators.note: the opening word is read in reverse

parts.note: a door is an opening

explanation.surface: A book's main character: a twisted edition with its opening turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwin Drood is the title character of Dickens's unfinished last novel.
